findings.title: Delete and Pause menu items never render in the list view
findings.body: The abilities for delete and pause are now computed from promRule, so canDelete and canPause can be true in the list view. But the Delete item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`, and the Pause item (line 123) is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. In the list view rulerRule is always undefined, so users with delete or pause permission never see those actions. The Delete handler also still requires a RulerRuleDTO to call handleDelete(rulerRule, ...), so the delete flow is not wired to the Grafana prom rule path at all.

findings.title: Pause action gated on rulerRule, which is absent in the list view
findings.body: canPause is computed from grafanaPauseAbility (promRule-based), but the MenuItemPauseRule is only rendered when `rulerRule` is a Grafana ruler rule. In the list view rulerRule is undefined, so the pause item is silently dropped even when the user is allowed to pause.

findings.title: Silence drawer never opens from the list view
findings.body: The Silence menu item is shown when canSilence is true (now derived from promRule), and clicking it calls setShowSilenceDrawer(true). But SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` holds, and rule is undefined in the list view. The click therefore does nothing.

findings.title: Grafana rule list item rendered without a key
findings.body: The previous GrafanaRuleLoader element had `key={key}`, and the diff removes it while rendering GrafanaRuleListItem. The list items are rendered from an array, so React will warn about missing keys. Reconciliation can also mix up rows when the list grows or re-sorts. The other branches in this switch still pass key.

findings.title: Federated rule group check removed from ruler abilities
findings.body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities now hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO. The previous useAllAlertRuleAbilities used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), so federated Mimir rule groups were treated as immutable (no edit, delete, pause or duplicate). Now they are shown as editable and deletable. Note that this hook also serves the data source rule path through AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons, so the regression is not limited to Grafana rules.

findings.title: View link drops the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader built the href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })`, which lets the rule view page navigate back to the list. The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops returnTo, so the view page loses the back-navigation context for rules opened from the list.

findings.title: Test asserts the buggy menu contents, hiding the missing Delete item
findings.body: The test grants AlertingRuleDelete and then asserts exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export). That expectation locks in the regression where Delete is never rendered in the list view. The test should expect Delete (and Pause where applicable), and it should check that the action performs the expected behaviour, not just that the items exist. The tests for silence also do not verify that the drawer opens.
